title: Edge VPC + KMS/HSM operator flow — UX spike notes
content:
Goal: quick, operator-focused console flows for connecting customer VPCs to a private Redwood control plane, configuring KMS/HSM, and validating network/region reachability. This doc is a low-fidelity UX spike + backlog seed — capture open questions, error states, and acceptance criteria for a follow-up design pass.

Context and audience:
- Primary: infra/platform engineers at customer orgs who manage networking and key material.
- Secondary: Redwood on-call/SEs doing initial setup or troubleshooting.
- Constraint: customers often cannot share internal CIDRs or extra credentials; flows must allow offline handoff and support air-gapped validation artifacts.

Key operator tasks covered:
1) Create a private deployment entry in Console (name, target region(s), SLA tier).
2) Establish network connectivity: VPC peering / Transit Gateway / VPN tunnel / private link.
3) Install and verify a lightweight site agent (optional for on-prem).
4) Connect KMS/HSM: IAM credentials, key ARN, certificate upload, attestation verification.
5) Region routing and fallback policy selection (prefer local region -> fallback region).
6) Run preflight checks and generate an operator bundle for offline handoff.

High-level flow (operator-first wireframe ideas):
- Step 0: Start: "New Private Deployment" modal (name + quick checklist). Minimal fields up front. CTA: "Create placeholder and continue setup".
- Step 1: Deployment overview with two big action tiles: "Network" and "Key material". Each tile shows status: Not started / In progress / Verified / Warning / Failed.
- Step 2: Network tile click -> network modes picker (Peering | TGW | Managed VPN | PrivateLink). Short explanations inline: e.g., "Peering: low-latency, single-region; TGW: multi-VPC; VPN: for firewall-only setups".
- Step 3: Mode-specific guided panels. For VPN: show preshared key generation, sample customer-side configuration snippets (Cisco/Juniper/Cloud Routers). For Peering: list required CIDR ranges and routing hints.
- Step 4: Agent instructions (if chosen) with checksum for binary and one-line curl install with token. Option to download offline bundle (tar + instructions).
- Step 5: KMS/HSM panel: two paths — Cloud KMS (provide IAM role or key ARN) vs. On-prem HSM (certificate upload + PKCS11 config). Provide a short attestation checklist and test-sign endpoint.
- Step 6: Preflight: single click to run remote checks (TCP handshake to specific IPs/ports, egress to our control plane, TLS cert fingerprint check, KMS sign test). Return a concise report with quick remediation links.

Microcopy and error state suggestions (operator tone, terse):
- Preflight banner: "Running connectivity checks — this may take up to 90s. Results will appear below."
- Error toast: "Network validation failed: route to 10.11.0.0/16 not found. Check customer route tables and return to retry."
- KMS error: "Key access denied — verify IAM role ARN and trust relationship (see example policy)."
- HSM error: "Certificate chain invalid — cert must contain CN and be PEM encoded. Upload again or use offline attestation."

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Operator can create a private deployment stub and save minimal metadata.
- Console offers 3 network modes with tailored instructions and produces a downloadable artifact for the customer network team.
- KMS flow supports at least AWS KMS (role ARN) and an HSM certificate upload surface for PKCS#11 config.
- Preflight returns pass/fail for network and key auth checks and stores a timestamped report.
- UI surfaces exact remediation steps per failed check and links to relevant docs.

Backlog/grooming tickets (seeded):
- PD-501: Network mode picker + mode-specific instructions + sample configs.
- PD-502: Preflight test runner + result viewer + downloadable diagnostic bundle.
- PD-503: KMS role link flow with policy templates and test-sign API call.
- PD-504: HSM certificate onboarding flow + PKCS11 field + attestation playback.
- PD-505: Agent offline bundle generator + checksum + install script.
- PD-506: Region fallback policy UI + per-region latency estimate.

Edge cases & operator notes:
- Customer has overlapping CIDR with Redwood-managed CIDR: surface conflict early, offer NAT tunnel option or suggest a DR region.
- No outbound internet allowed from customer network: provide an offline attest bundle and clear manual steps for secure import.
- HSM manufacturer differences: show vendor-specific notes (Thales, Utimaco) and allow uploading of vendor module configs.
- Key rotation: require rotation window and show a step-by-step of dual-write window for safe rollovers.

Wireframe sketches (textual, low-fi):
- Dashboard card layout: left column: deployment metadata + action buttons. Middle: big stepper with Network -> Agent -> Keys -> Preflight -> Go-live. Right column: status timeline + recent checks + contact SE.
- Network panel mock: 3 columns (Instructions | Sample snippets | Quick test). Quick test is a terminal-like box showing a simulated curl/telnet attempt and a green/red LED next to each check.

Operational runbook snippets for SE/on-call:
- If preflight shows TLS mismatch: capture the certificate fingerprint and ask customer to run openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -showcerts and paste output into support case.
- If KMS test-sign fails with AccessDenied: ask for assume-role policy JSON and a CloudTrail event timeframe.
- If HSM attestation fails: request vendor audit logs and the device serial; escalate to security for manual verification.

Open questions for product/design review:
- Do we surface vendor-specific HSM configs in UI or keep that in docs + attachable config files? (security stance: minimal UI surface is preferred, but operators appreciate inline hints).
- Should preflight run automatically on every change or require explicit click? Tradeoff: noisy checks vs. stale state.
- Offline bundles: what is the minimum artifact set we should produce to make handoff painless? (certs, sample cloud router configs, a validation script, and a README).

Proposed next steps (short-term):
- UX: produce 2 high-fidelity wireframes for network panel and KMS onboarding by EOD next week.
- Eng: prototype preflight health-check runner as a Lambda-like job with pluggable checks. Hook a simple API to return structured results.
- Docs: draft sample IAM policy for AWS KMS assume-role and a short vendor-agnostic HSM checklist.
- Schedule: sync with SE (Marcus) and SRE (Rahul) to validate sample router snippets and port lists.

Notes / decisions log:
- 2025-09-14: decided to prioritize AWS KMS and generic PKCS11 HSM support for MVP — additional cloud KMS providers TBD. (A. Patel)
- 2025-09-16: offline bundle format: tar.gz with README + certs + test scripts. Keep signing tokens short-lived (1h). (S. Alvarez)

Quick copy snippets for UI (for handoff):
- Setup step header: "Connect your network and key material"
- Network CTA: "Generate network bundle"
- KMS CTA: "Verify key access"
- Preflight PASS state: "All checks passed — ready to schedule Go-live"
- Preflight FAIL state: "One or more checks failed — expand for details"

This is intentionally terse and operationally focused. Use this as the source of truth for the grooming session; please add comments inline or drop issues into the PD backlog.

TODOs (quick):
- [ ] Get vendor PKCS11 samples from SE (Marcus)
- [ ] Draft assume-role policy template (Rahul)
- [ ] UX small pass: clarify offline bundle copy (Aisha)
- [ ] Add HSM vendor notes to docs (Sofia)

End of spike notes.
